Senses.Explanation: Literally, one stalk or blade of grass. The Chan corpus loads this smallest ordinary object through a set of reversible public formulas. Most prominently, a master may 'take a single blade of grass and make it a sixteen-foot golden body, and take the sixteen-foot golden body and make it a single blade of grass.' The same blade can found a monastery or display jeweled halls and jade palaces. Baiyun Duan's saying makes the relation reversible: after one true sweat, jeweled halls appear atop a blade of grass; without it, even jeweled halls are covered by the blade. Dahui accepts the first clause but warns that the second may deceive the hearer. A separate inherited encounter supplies another deployment: Sudhana picks a blade of grass from the ground as the medicine requested by Manjusri, who says that this medicine can kill and can give life. The Chan-specific bend lies in how the records repeatedly place the concrete blade in reversible comparison with a buddha-body, a monastery, palaces, and medicine, while later masters quote, test, and qualify those formulas.
Senses.Note: Zen-allowlist count: 617 hits in 174 texts. Searches covered the golden-body reversal, monastery erection, palace manifestation/covering, medicine case, later qualification, and ordinary botanical use. Family check with the sixteen-foot golden body (丈六金身), monastery (梵剎), jeweled halls and jade palaces (瓊樓玉殿), medicine (藥), and mustard seed (芥子) supports one concrete blade deployed in distinct comparisons, not separate referents; no split.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拈一莖草作丈六金身，將丈六金身作一莖草
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 列祖提綱錄. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Mi'an Xianjie as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善財遂於地上拈一莖草，度與文殊。殊接得，示眾曰：此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 宗門拈古彙集. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Sudhana as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何能拈一莖草作丈六金身，插一莖草而建梵剎，向一莖草上現瓊樓玉殿耶？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 千巖和尚語錄. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Qianyan Yuanzhang as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若端的得一回汗出，便向一莖草上現出瓊樓玉殿；若未端的得一回汗出，縱有瓊樓玉殿，被一莖草葢却。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄), in Chushi Fanqi's later raising. Chushi explicitly introduces Baiyun Shouduan's instruction with '白雲端和尚示眾云'; Baiyun Shouduan is the exact quoted speaker who says that after truly sweating once, jeweled halls appear on a single blade of grass, while otherwise a blade of grass covers even jeweled halls. Chushi's own comment begins only at '師云'.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一莖草上現瓊樓玉殿。決定可信。瓊樓玉殿被一莖草蓋却。莫被他熱謾。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui affirms the palace appearing on grass but warns against being deceived by the reverse clause.
